# 150 Winter Wildlife Video Prompts for Seedance 2.0 — Set 2 (USA & Canada)

15-second, 9:16, smartphone-style prompts set in real snowy, icy and freezing locations across the United States and Canada. Each one has a 0–2 second hook, a second-by-second timeline, natural sound only, and the 12-section structure below. They are written for Seedance 2.0 with Seedance 2.5-level realism as the target.

**Every prompt contains these sections, in this order:** FORMAT · LOOK · CAMERA · LOCATION · CHARACTERS · HOOK (00:00–00:02) · TIMELINE (00:00–00:15, second by second) · SOUND DESIGN · AUDIO REALISM · 4K/8K VISUAL QUALITY ENHANCEMENT · REALISM AND CONTINUITY · AVOID

**Ground rules for all 150:** wildlife and nature only, with no rescue scenarios and no people handling animals. Native North American species, natural sound only (no music, voiceover or dialogue), one continuous handheld phone take, and no repeats of each other, of the four reference clips, or of the earlier 150-prompt set.

Copy a prompt with the copy button on its code block.

**Subject:** A muskrat pushing up through a small snowy "push-up" feeding hut on the marsh ice and sitting at its doorway eating a cattail root, until a common raven lands on the push-up's roof and tries to steal from it, two skiers on a dike trail  
**Length:** 7,110 characters

```text

LOCATION:
A marsh pool at Seney National Wildlife Refuge in Michigan's Upper Peninsula: a snowy dike trail, frozen pools full of cattails, scattered muskrat push-ups and lodges, and boreal forest of tamarack and jack pine beyond.

A muskrat; a common raven; the filmer, a woman in her 40s in a teal ski jacket and a white headband; her partner, a man in a red anorak, standing on skis beside her.

In the middle of a frozen marsh, a small snowy mound has a little door in its side — and a furry face pops out with breakfast, then a raven lands right on its roof.

TIMELINE:

00:13–00:14 — The muskrat settles back in its doorway and resumes chewing the root, its whiskers flicking.

AUDIO REALISM:
Pure on-device phone audio: the built-in mic's limited low end, mild compression, and automatic gain that briefly pumps when something loud happens. Gusts cause short mic-rumble pops, then clear.
```
